jobs.title: Content Creator - YouTube
jobs.jd_full:
Important: Applications without an intro video will not be considered.


Job Overview

Create engaging YouTube tutorials about software, digital marketing, and AI tools that reach millions of people around the world every month through our YouTube channel, Metics Media.


About us

Metics Media is a small, fully remote team creating high-quality YouTube videos about software, digital marketing, and AI tools for an audience of over 700,000 subscribers. Our mission is simple: to make technology easy to understand and help people get the most out of the tools available to them.

We partner with leading platforms like Shopify, Hostinger, and Squarespace, allowing us to keep our content free and accessible to everyone.

We're now looking for talented, motivated content creators to join our growing team, help us produce even more high-quality videos, and reach millions more people around the world.


What you'll do
  • Research each video's topic and tools in depth, and figure out what to cover and how to present it in a clear, engaging way.
  • Write video scripts and outlines.
  • Record videos, including talking-head and screen recordings. Your face will be visible in your videos.
  • Perform basic video editing tasks and prepare footage for our in-house editor.


What we're looking for
  • Native-level written and spoken English
  • Strong on-camera presentation skills and the ability to communicate clearly and confidently
  • Ability to quickly understand complex topics and explain them clearly to beginners
  • Strong research skills and the ability to verify information before presenting it
  • AI-native and highly proficient with modern AI tools, using them effectively to work faster, improve quality, and maximize productivity
  • High attention to detail and a strong commitment to producing high-quality work
  • Ability to take feedback and continuously improve
  • Reliable, organized, and able to work independently and take ownership of your projects
  • Genuine interest in YouTube, online tools, software, and learning new topics
  • A quiet, dedicated workspace where you can work without interruptions, with room to set up a small studio for recording talking-head videos with minimal background noise
  • Fast internet connection with at least 50 Mbps download and 25 Mbps upload
  • Legal authorization to work in the US or Canada


Nice to have
  • Previous experience creating educational video content
  • Knowledge of topics such as website creation, AI tools, ecommerce, or other areas we regularly create videos about
  • Equipment needed to produce high-quality videos


Working at Metics Media

At Metics Media, you'll have a lot of freedom in how you work. You'll be trusted to structure your own day, manage your projects independently, and take ownership of your work. We're a small, ambitious team with high standards, and we're always looking for ways to improve what we create and how we work.

At the same time, you'll get hands-on support, feedback, and training from people with over 8 years of experience making YouTube videos.


Compensation
  • Base salary: $70,000 USD per year (US) / CA$80,000 per year (Canada)
  • Profit sharing: Earn a percentage of the profit generated by every video you create, paid out quarterly
  • For reference, our current creators have earned an average total compensation (base salary + profit-sharing bonuses) of $85,000 USD in their first year and $155,000 USD in their second year. These figures are based on the past performance of our current creator team and are not guaranteed.


Benefits
  • 15 days of paid vacation per year, plus public holidays
  • 10 paid sick days per year
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • A 401(k) with employer contributions (US)


How to apply

Applications require a short intro video (max. 5 minutes) and your CV. Click "Apply" for all details.

jobs.title: Workforce Management - Real Time Analyst
jobs.jd_full:
About Clipboard

Our mission is to uplift as many communities as possible. We do this through our app-based marketplace that connects healthcare professionals with the workplaces that need amazing workers. This enables hundreds of thousands of people to achieve financial stability for themselves and their families while providing essential care to millions of people across the U.S.

Founded in 2016, we are a remote-first team of over 1,000 people building a top Y-Combinator company and have been profitable since 2022. We’re the leader in Long-Term Care staffing and are rapidly expanding into Home Health, Hospitals, and more, meaning we have more work to do than people to do it, and are growing our team to support millions more people and their communities.

Overview

📍 Remote Global - Central and South America

We are seeking a WFM Central - Real Time Analyst to serve as the central governance layer for live operations across multiple Lines of Business (LoB). This is not a traditional monitoring role; it is designed for a high-caliber, forensic operator who functions as an operational architect. You will be a trusted partner to operational leadership, responsible for continuing to evolve our operations to a standardized, and fiscally sound control model.

The ideal candidate possesses the technical "know-how" of a forensic analyst and the communication prowess of a business consultant, capable of telling a compelling story through data to stakeholders ranging from Team Leads to Directors. You won't just report that a queue is at risk; you will diagnose the business impact, identify the root cause, and prescribe the specific levers leadership must pull to preserve SLA and the customer experience. You will be the owner of all aspects of the support queues and ensure we are meeting our customers where they need us.

Responsibilities

  • Stakeholder Storytelling: Distill complex, "noisy" operational signals into high-impact narratives. You must be able to share in-depth observations and supporting data that tell a clear story to stakeholders, at all levels of leadership, on exactly what actions must be taken.

  • Business-Level Analysis: Go beyond the "what" and the "why" to analyze long-term business trends. Evaluate the financial efficiency of SLA safeguarding and the fiscal impact of current staffing vs. demand density.

  • Operational Control & Forensic Auditing: Serve as the authoritative "voice of reason" during incidents. Conduct forensic audits of agent behaviors such as "On Hold" abuse or status irregularities to ensure hidden capacity drains are eliminated.

  • Centralized Core Governance: Enact queue management playbooks for real-time levers across multiple LoBs, ensuring aggressive SLAs are preserved through structured accountability.

  • Strategic Planning & Optimization: Partner with WFM to create a concise feedback loop for continued improvement in planning and scheduling.

Qualifications

  • Exceptional Communication: Proven ability to translate complex data into a clear jargon-free business story. You must be comfortable presenting actionable insights to senior leadership under high-pressure conditions.

  • Advanced Forensic Analysis: Expert proficiency in Google Sheets is required, familiarity with Metabase preferred. You must be able to build complex, automated tracking tools and forensic audits from scratch. Not just for basic queue health, but also analyzing business data that influences our operations.

  • Strategic Judgment: Demonstrated experience making high-judgment decisions that impact the entire business, particularly in environments with aggressive SLAs and fluctuating volume patterns.

  • Operational Architecture: Take ownership in documenting best practices into governed frameworks and playbooks.

  • Resilient Mindset: Comfortable operating autonomously in a 24/7 environment, with the flexibility to adapt to operational needs as part of a high-impact, interdependent team.

  • Systems Fluency: Familiarity with Amazon Connect, Zendesk Omnichannel routing, and Assembled WFM is highly preferred.

What Success Looks Like

  • Operational anomalies are quickly investigated, with root causes clearly identified and communicated, reducing repeat issues and leadership uncertainty

  • You evolve queue management processes from reactive to a documented, standardized, and predictive operating model.

  • Champion of the team’s brand with Operational Leadership. You are looked to as the primary source of truth, relying on your data-driven stories to make critical staffing and operational decisions.

  • Live queues remain stable, governed, and resilient across all supported lines of business, even during unexpected spikes, outages, or incidents

  • Stakeholders receive timely, clear updates during incidents that explain impact, cause, and corrective actions in a concise and actionable manner.

Hiring Process

  • Application

  • Intro Call with Recruiter

  • Case Study

  • Interview with Central WFM - RTA Team Lead

  • Interview with Queue Operations Manager - Core Services

  • Interview with Head of Core Services

  • Final Culture Interview with Executive Leadership

Quick Note on Scammers:

Clipboard would never ask you for money or your bank details to participate in our hiring process. Report any scammers impersonating the Clipboard hiring team members here.

About Amplify

The Amplify Classroom platform combines curriculum, assessment, and supplemental learning into one coherent high-quality instructional system. A pioneer in education since 2000, Amplify has developed deep relationships in states and districts by partnering with educators to drive implementation quality and improved outcomes. Today, Amplify serves more than 18 million students and teachers across all 50 states and on six continents. For more information, visit Amplify.com.

Description:

The Revenue Systems Analyst is the connective tissue between Revenue Systems, the overall Revenue Operations team, and the Business Systems team. This role leads structured process discovery, maps current and future state workflows, and translates operational needs into clear, testable requirements for Business Systems and other partners, with a focus on business clarity rather than system configuration. The focus of the Revenue Systems team is improving seller and sales-operations execution across lead-to-cash (quoting, contracting, ordering, invoicing, renewals/amendments), reducing rework, strengthening data integrity, sales finance/ budgeting, and accelerating change adoption.

This role also supports the strategy, administration, and adoption of the platforms that power revenue workflows, including our market intelligence platform. Success in this role depends less on producing documents than on the human work behind them, building trust with business partners, asking the questions that surface what people actually do versus what the process says they do, and driving decisions across teams that don't always agree. This is not a system administration or configuration role.

Essential Responsibilities:

Business Process Discovery and Design

  • Facilitate workshops and working sessions with key stakeholders (Account Executives, District Managers, Sales Support, Renewals, Sales Finance, and Business Systems) to document current state end-to-end business processes and define improved future state designs facilitated by systems and process improvements.

  • Create clear, multi-level process maps (e.g., lead-to-quote, quote-to-contract, order-to-cash, renewals/amendments) that reflect real seller and operations workflows, handoffs, approvals, and exception paths.

  • Establish and maintain a lightweight process library (maps, SOPs, definitions, decision trees) so institutional knowledge is durable and scalable.

Requirements and Solution Definition (Sales and Sales Operations Lens)

  • Translate process and policy decisions into well-structured requirements: user stories, acceptance criteria, business rules, and operational scenarios - ensuring clarity, completeness, and testability.

  • Partner with Business Systems to validate feasibility, clarify ambiguities, and ensure requirements reflect both the operational intent and system constraints.

  • Maintain traceability from process maps -> requirements -> test cases -> release notes to reduce rework and ensure end-to-end quality.

  • Use AI-powered tools (e.g., Glean, Claude, Gemini) to accelerate drafting of user stories, business cases, acceptance criteria, process documentation, and stakeholder synthesis — applying judgment to validate accuracy, completeness, and business fit rather than accepting output at face value.

Tools Strategy and Administration

  • Support the administration and strategy development of the platforms supporting revenue workflows, including our market intelligence platform, assisting in configuration, user access, adoption tracking, and vendor coordination.

  • Translate market intelligence signals into usable seller and sales-operations workflows, partnering with Business Systems on data flow, attribution, and reporting integration.

  • Build and maintain enablement resources (playbooks, prompt libraries, use case guides) that drive consistent, high-value usage across the field.

  • Evaluate, pilot, and operationalize additional platforms as needed, including AI-enabled solutions, and make recommendations on fit, sequencing, and expansion.

Operational Readiness, Testing, and Change Enablement

  • Co-design UAT approaches and test scenarios rooted in real-world seller and Sales Operations use cases; coordinate execution with Business Systems and key business testers.

  • Develop end-user documentation (job aids, playbooks, process guides) and support enablement activities to drive adoption and consistent execution.

  • Support release readiness by confirming training, communications, reporting impacts, and operational 'go-live' checklists are complete.

Continuous Improvement and Performance Insights

  • Use operational data and qualitative feedback to identify friction points, bottlenecks, policy leakage, and process variability - and recommend improvements.

  • Support defining process KPIs (cycle time, rework/defect rates, adoption, SLA attainment) and partner with reporting teams to surface actionable insights.

  • Promote standardization and simplification while preserving necessary state/district/contracting complexity through clear guardrails and exception handling.

  • Evaluate emerging technologies, automation opportunities, and AI-enabled solutions that can simplify workflows, reduce manual effort, and improve operational effectiveness.

Cross-Functional Partnership and Governance

  • Act as a neutral facilitator to align Sales, Finance, and Business Systems on process decisions, definitions, and sequencing - especially in quoting, contracting, ordering, and invoicing workflows.

  • Support governance routines (change intake, prioritization, documentation standards, decision logs) to keep cross-functional work moving and reduce 'spin.'

  • Contribute to program initiatives across the revenue systems roadmap (e.g., quoting modernization, amendments/contracting improvements, data governance, commission and budget operationalization, seller enablement).

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Operations, or related field (or equivalent experience).

  • 4+ years of experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Business Process Analysis, or related roles focused on process design and operational improvement.

  • Demonstrated ability to create process maps and documentation that non-technical audiences can follow (e.g., Lucidchart, Visio, Miro, or similar).

  • Experience translating business needs into clear requirements (user stories, acceptance criteria, business rules) and supporting cross-functional delivery.

  • Experience working with CRM and revenue operations platforms (Salesforce preferred) and familiarity with lead-to-cash processes including quoting, contracting, ordering, invoicing, and renewals.

  • Strong facilitation, stakeholder management, and written communication skills; comfortable driving alignment across teams with competing priorities.

  • Analytical mindset and comfort using data to diagnose issues and validate improvements.

  • Demonstrated curiosity and willingness to learn new technologies, methodologies, and ways of working, including the use of AI-powered tools to improve productivity, process design, analysis, documentation, and decision-making.

Travel required (about 10-15%).

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in K-12 education, EdTech, or other subscription/SaaS environments with complex contracting and renewal processes.

  • Experience with CRMs and Quoting automation and contract/amendment workflows (e.g., Salesforce CPQ / Revenue Cloud/ or similar) from an operational design perspective.

  • Lean / Six Sigma (Green Belt or higher), PMP, or comparable process improvement training.

  • Familiarity with Agile delivery practices, backlog hygiene, and tools like Jira/Confluence (or equivalent).

  • Experience building playbooks/SOPs and partnering with enablement teams to drive adoption in the field.

You will also continuously scan the organization to spot where new process infrastructure is needed (and equally, where existing process should be retired or simplified).

The right person for this role has spent a career proving that great process is a force multiplier — not bureaucracy — and has the instinct to feel the line between too much process and too little, and to stay on the right side of it.

Responsibilities:

1. Planning & Roadmapping

Co-design and steward the cross-functional planning calendar for the Product organization — coordinating annual planning cycles, aligned artifacts, delivery expectations, and planned moments of alignment with Sales and GTM. The calendar that actually gets used is the one the people running it helped shape; you build it with Suite Leads, the Resource Allocation team, and GTM partners — not in a vacuum.

  • Resolve the misalignment that exists today — inconsistent work planning methodologies across suites, mismatched planning timeframes (platform, digital product, and suites all on different cadences), lack of backward planning for cross-team dependencies, and rolling release cycles out of sync with the school year — by introducing the lightest framework that genuinely solves the problem.

  • Maintain dynamic business unit and cross-product roadmaps and ensure alignment across all other planning functions, building shared visibility into where the portfolio is headed and how dependencies fit together.

2. End-to-End Launch Planning & Related Processes

  • Design the standardized end-to-end launch process across business units — including launch readiness checklists, health checks, cross-stakeholder touchpoints, release documentation, and clean flow of data from product to supply chain.

  • Co-develop the launch playbook with Go-To-Market, Sales, Customer Experience, Marketing, and Supply Chain — building it with the functions executing against it, not imposing it on them. The teams who run launches today have hard-won knowledge; your job is to surface and codify it, not overwrite it.

  • Codify ready-to-launch protocols that ensure pricing is finalized, manufacturing and distribution are confirmed, market collateral is approved, and Sales and CX teams are fully enabled — every time, regardless of which suite is launching, and without adding meaningful overhead to the teams doing the work.

3. Stage Gates & Decision Frameworks

  • Steward and continuously evolve the five-gate stage gate process that the organization is currently rolling out — including the differentiated tracks (e.g., new programs, new markets, in-market management) so that gating is right-sized to the investment and not a one-size-fits-all forcing function.

  • Co-develop refinements with suite leaders and stage gate sponsors as pilots (Science V2, CA K-8 Literacy, and others) generate real-world learnings. The gate process should feel like it belongs to the people running it, not like compliance imposed from outside the suite.

  • Manage gate review orchestration — scheduling, materials, decision documentation, and tracking — so decisions made in stage gate meetings actually stick. You stop the “decisions get unmade” pattern that has dogged the org, without turning gate prep into a second job for the teams.

  • Own scope change management — the process for evaluating and approving changes after a gate has been passed — so the organization can respond to legitimate new information without descending into the “culture of yes” that erodes delivery.

  • Partner with Finance & Analytics to link funding and resourcing decisions to gate readiness, helping deliver against the 2026 KPI that 60% of 2027 R&D spend is vetted through stage gates or an independent strategic framework.

4. Spot Gaps and Build Lightweight, Co-Developed Process

  • Identify new areas where process infrastructure is needed: you scan the organization continuously — listening to Suite Leads, project managers, and shared services about where work is breaking down — and you triage where new process is genuinely the answer (versus better tools, clearer ownership, or simply leaving things alone).

  • Build process that earns its keep: your default is the lightest possible framework that solves the problem at hand. You instinctively distinguish between rigor that protects delivery and overhead that drains it, and you reach for the former without slipping into the latter.

  • Retire and simplify as actively as you create. When a process isn’t working, you change it; when a process isn’t needed, you retire it. You see the absence of a framework as a hypothesis to test, not a mandate to fill.

  • Build and lead the central team that designs, iterates on, and supports critical processes and associated tools and templates — while making sure business units have what they need to execute consistently.

  • Establish a continuous improvement loop — instrumenting the processes you own, learning from pilots, and iterating quickly based on what you (and the people doing the work) observe in the field.

Who You Are…

  • A Lightweight-First Process Designer: Your instinct is always toward the lightest framework that solves the problem. You see overhead as a tax on delivery, and you have the judgment to know when more process is the answer and when it isn’t. You can feel the line between too much and too little process — and you stay on the right side of it.

  • A Co-Creator, Not an Imposer: You build process with the people who will live with it. You start every engagement with deep listening — to suite leaders, PMs, designers, content leads — and you ship frameworks that feel like extensions of how teams already work, not corrections imposed from above.

  • A Gap-Spotter: You actively scan the organization for places where process infrastructure could unlock impact — and equally for places where existing process should be simplified or retired. You triage thoughtfully: not every gap needs a framework, and not every framework is worth keeping.

  • An Operator’s Operator: You have run real launches, real planning cycles, and real stage gates — and you bring that experiential credibility to every conversation with suite leaders. You know what overhead feels like from the receiving end, which is why you’re so careful not to create more of it.

  • A Continuous Improver: You see every pilot as a learning opportunity, every miss as a signal, and every win as a stepping stone. You instrument your work and let the data — and the people doing the work — guide refinement.

  • An Expert Navigator: You know how to build influence across a matrixed organization to get things done without formal authority. You are the person leaders trust to make a fair call when process and urgency are in tension.

  • Demonstrated track record of building lightweight, well-adopted process: frameworks that teams actually use rather than binders that gather dust. Bonus points if you can point to a process you deliberately simplified or retired.

  • Track record of leading cross-functional product launches end-to-end — including the GTM, Sales, CX, Marketing, and Supply Chain coordination that turn a “ready to ship” product into a successful one in market.

Temporal is used by a lot of companies in a wide variety of contexts. Many use Temporal Cloud. Many others users don’t yet know about Temporal Cloud, believe self-hosting is cheaper, and/or just don’t yet see a need to move. Still others (often happily using Temporal Cloud at large scale) also operate environments where a managed service isn't an option today and may never be, like:

  • AI and application companies embedding Temporal inside software their own customers run in isolated, air-gapped environments, or offering a remote management BYOA posture

  • Large enterprises keeping operational control of critical systems in-house by policy

  • Companies operating in sovereign clouds and similar contexts where legal or organizational requirements make outside management difficult or impossible

This role owns understanding the world of Temporal usage outside Cloud, what the different contexts demand, and where Temporal should (and shouldn't) engage. That includes what we build, what we support, what we charge for, and what we leave alone. You'll shape which offerings we pursue and how they make money or contribute to the larger business. Then you'll take the ones we commit to through launch and adoption.

Open source Temporal is central to this. We’re investing heavily in OSS, from performance improvements to easier management to clearer guidance on compatibility and cost. When companies write their apps on Temporal, they’re making a huge bet on us, and that trust is sacred. A large part of this role is improving and shepherding how we keep making OSS better.

What You’ll Do

  • Map usage outside Temporal Cloud. Build the company's clearest picture of where Temporal runs outside Cloud and why.   • Decide what we pursue. Recommend which needs deserve new offerings, which Temporal Cloud should cover, and which we deliberately leave alone. Write the case, defend it, and revisit it when the evidence changes.

  • Define the line between open source and paid. Set clear guidelines for which improvements and support go into open source Temporal, and where paid offerings take over. Keep the open source experience strong, and make the line easy for users and internal teams to understand.

  • Define the business model. Work with leadership, Sales, and Finance on packaging, pricing, and how we sell offerings that run outside our infrastructure. Know what customers will pay for and what it costs us to support it.

  • Help Cloud win where it should. Work with other PMs so workloads that can run on Cloud move there more easily, with a clear value and TCO case.

  • Lead without authority. Align Engineering, Resident Architects, Dev Success, Security, and go-to-market teams, including when their incentives conflict.

  • Own outcomes. Define success in terms of adoption, revenue, and retention. Use the results to steer further investment.

  • Experience with infrastructure or platform products that customers operate themselves: open source, on-prem, or hybrid.

External Relationship Management & Primary Funder Point of Contact

Ideal Candidate Profile

Experience

Skills

  • Outstanding interpersonal and relationship-building skills; comfortable pitching, negotiating, and presenting to executive-level external partners.
  • Pragmatic problem-solving capability; able to de-escalate partner concerns quickly with clear, executable action plans.
  • Strong written communication and storytelling skills—able to break down complex projects, provide necessary context, and write clear, compelling funder reports, progress updates, meeting notes, and contribute to renewal proposals.
  • Advanced financial acumen with proficiency in tracking project burn rates, budget variance, and resource allocation.

Personal Attributes

  • Natural relationship-builder & professional—approachable, diplomatic, and articulate when engaging external funders and internal teammates alike.
  • Proactive "doer" & problem-solver—energized by tackling operational friction, taking ownership of tasks, and getting cross-functional deliverables over the finish line.

  • Strong narrative thinker—possesses the clarity of thought and writing discipline to explain the "why" and "so what" behind project milestones, ensuring external partners grasp the full context of our work.
  • Mission-driven with a passion for digital literacy, education, and empowering youth across Canada.

If this sounds like you - we want to hear from you!

Qui sommes-nous?

Depuis 2013, Digital Moment est un chef de file en éducation numérique auprès des jeunes canadiens. Chaque année, nous élargissons la portée et l’impact de nos programmes..

Mais nous ne nous arrêtons pas là. Nous innovons continuellement afin de donner aux jeunes les compétences nécessaires pour tirer parti des technologies émergentes et relever certains des défis sociaux les plus urgents de notre époque.

Grâce à nos programmes et initiatives novateurs, nous contribuons à former une génération de leaders qui maîtrisent l’intelligence artificielle et qui sont prêts à bâtir le Canada de demain.

Notre travail repose sur trois valeurs fondamentales : l’innovation, l’inclusion et l’impact. Nous donnons à la prochaine génération les moyens de façonner la technologie pour le bien collectif. Travailler chez Digital Moment, c’est avoir l’occasion de faire une différence chaque jour en donnant aux jeunes les compétences numériques essentielles pour évoluer dans un monde où la technologie occupe une place centrale.

Nous sommes une petite équipe, dynamique et ambitieuse, qui travaille entièrement à distance. Nous valorisons l’innovation, remettons en question les façons de faire établies et expérimentons avec de nouvelles idées afin de créer des changements significatifs. Nous avons bâti une culture positive et collaborative, axée sur la mission et l’impact que nous souhaitons créer.

Nous sommes actuellement à la recherche d’un·e gestionnaire senior de projets pour se joindre à notre équipe.

Aperçu du poste

Vous serez la principale personne-ressource auprès de nos bailleurs de fonds nationaux, partenaires corporatifs et partenaires de projets partout au Canada. Dans ce rôle, vous mettrez à profit votre forte expertise en gestion de projets et vos aptitudes exceptionnelles en développement de relations afin de gérer nos initiatives les plus complexes, impliquant de multiples parties prenantes, de leur conception jusqu’à leur finition.

Vous veillerez à ce que tous nos engagements organisationnels soient respectés dans les délais, selon la portée prévue et dans les limites budgétaires établies.

Notre culture organisationnelle est hautement collaborative et axée sur l’action : chez Digital Moment, tout le monde met la main à la pâte pour faire avancer les choses. Vous êtes à la fois une personne stratégique, capable de résoudre des problèmes complexes, et une personne d’action qui aime passer de la planification à l’exécution. Vous excellez à transformer des engagements complexes envers les bailleurs de fonds en plans de projets structurés, à bâtir des relations authentiques avec nos partenaires externes et à intervenir directement dans la réalisation des livrables aux côtés des équipes internes.

Principales responsabilités

Gestion des relations externes et rôle principal auprès des bailleurs de fonds

  • Agir comme principale personne-ressource auprès des partenaires externes, bailleurs de fonds et partenaires corporatifs tout au long du cycle de vie des projets, en développant des relations chaleureuses, professionnelles et fondées sur la confiance.

Suivi financier, gestion du temps et exécution concrète — esprit d’action

  • Personne engagée envers la mission, passionnée par la littératie numérique, l’éducation et l’autonomisation des jeunes partout au Canada.

Fingerprint empowers enterprises to detect and stop online fraud with the world’s most accurate device intelligence.  We lead our industry with bleeding-edge identification capabilities and work on turning new ideas and discoveries in the fraud detection space into reality. Our customers range from innovative startups to leading enterprise companies, including Plaid, Dropbox, and Booking.com. 

Fingerprint is a globally dispersed, 100% remote company. We were named on on the 2026 Forbes Best Startup Employers list and ranked #803 on the 2026 Inc. 5000 list of America’s fastest-growing private companies. 

We have raised $77M and are backed by Craft Ventures (Tesla, Facebook, Airbnb ), Nexus Venture Partners ( Postman, Apollo.io, MinIO, Druva) and Uncorrelated Ventures ( Redis, Rollbar,  Gradle).

 

 

About the Role

Fingerprint is looking for a Technical Product Manager (P3) to help turn product strategy into clear, well-executed product delivery. This role is ideal for someone who is building strong product management fundamentals, enjoys working closely with engineering and design, and is energized by keeping product work organized, well-documented, and moving toward release.

In this role, you will own specific product features or workstreams under the guidance of a Sr Technical Product Manager. You will help translate product intent into clear user stories, jobs-to-be-done, acceptance criteria, release plans, documentation, and operational updates. You will work across Product, Engineering, Design, Product Analytics, Customer Success, Sales, and Product Marketing to ensure product records are accurate, dependencies are visible, stakeholders are informed, and shipped work meets the expected customer and business outcomes.

This role blends TPM expectations with the Delivery Product Owner operating model: the Sr TPM sets product direction, priorities, success metrics, and major tradeoffs; the TPM helps ensure that direction becomes shippable, well-understood, and well-supported product increments.

What you’ll do

Product delivery and execution

  • Own delivery coordination for specific product features, epics, or workstreams within priorities and constraints set by the Sr TPM.
  • Translate Sr TPM intent into clear user stories, jobs-to-be-done, acceptance criteria, and definitions of done.
  • Maintain Jira epics, tasks, acceptance criteria, and delivery status in partnership with Engineering.
  • Keep systems of record accurate and current, including Notion, Jira, Productboard, and relevant roadmap or release tracking tools.
  • Support backlog refinement, sprint-ready sequencing, and release readiness activities.
  • Track delivery risks, open questions, dependencies, and decisions; escalate when a change impacts goals, metrics, customer commitments, timeline, scope, pricing, eligibility, or cross-stakeholder priorities.
  • Attend technical reviews and build enough technical context to follow architecture, implementation, and tradeoff discussions.

Product documentation and communication

  • Create and maintain clear feature documentation with oversight from a more senior TPM.
  • Document product use cases and represent assigned feature use cases confidently with internal stakeholders.
  • Support PRDs by creating clear user stories, JTBD, acceptance criteria, and customer/business context for assigned features.
  • Draft or support internal release notes, product updates, and stakeholder communications.
  • Help ensure developer documentation is updated when product behavior changes.
  • Communicate feature status, known limitations, delivery timing, and release readiness to internal stakeholders.

Customer, market, and product insight

  • Monitor relevant customer feedback channels, support channels, Productboard insights, and internal stakeholder requests.
  • Create insights for issues that may qualify as product limitations or product improvements.
  • Participate in customer discovery, customer brainstorms, user experience discussions, and product feedback sessions.
  • Collect qualitative and quantitative data to support prioritization conversations.
  • Understand the competitive landscape for assigned product areas and stay aware of relevant technical or market developments.

Product operations and launch support

  • Help maintain roadmap and feature records as work progresses through lifecycle stages.
  • Support product launch readiness by coordinating across Engineering, Product Marketing, CS, Sales, and Support.
  • Assist Product Marketing with customer education materials, release communication, and launch artifacts.
  • Help prepare product updates for internal forums such as CS/SE syncs or release channels.
  • Track post-launch success metrics for epics and issues, and help summarize learnings for future iterations.

What success looks like

A successful TPM at Fingerprint:

  • Owns specific product features or workstreams reliably, while operating within product priorities set by a Sr TPM or product leader.
  • Creates clear, actionable user stories, JTBD, acceptance criteria, and feature documentation.
  • Keeps Jira, Notion, Productboard, and roadmap records accurate and up to date.
  • Understands the technical domain well enough to articulate the needs of technical personas and participate in technical discussions.
  • Reviews Jira epics, tasks, and acceptance criteria with the Team Lead and Sr TPM.
  • Understands engineering estimates and can communicate delivery implications to the appropriate internal stakeholders with support.
  • Talks about and demonstrates specific product features confidently to internal stakeholders.
  • Articulates the product roadmap and current feature priorities, including relevant business priorities and JTBD, with assistance.
  • Collects qualitative and quantitative inputs for prioritization decisions.
  • Understands success metrics for epics and issues and helps track metrics post-launch.
  • Escalates appropriately when a decision moves beyond delivery execution and affects customer promises, business outcomes, product metrics, pricing, eligibility, or strategic priority.

Requirements for Success

  • Experience in product management, product ownership, business or product analysis, technical program management, solutions or support engineering, or a similar role working with technical products such as APIs, SaaS platforms, developer tools, fraud prevention, security, or analytics.
  • Strong written communication skills, including creating structured product documentation, developer guides, and stakeholder updates.
  • Familiarity with agile product development, backlog management, release readiness, and cross-functional delivery workflows for API and data-centric products.
  • Ability to partner with Engineering and Design to clarify requirements, acceptance criteria, and user experience expectations; comfort reading technical documentation and discussing implementation details with engineers.
  • Ability to use product analytics, customer feedback, and stakeholder input to support product decisions, with experience using tools such as Productboard, Notion, Jira, Amplitude, Sigma, SQL, or similar systems.
  • Attention to detail, reliable follow-through, and ownership of operational details, with a bias toward making ambiguous work clearer for the team.
  • Curiosity about customer problems, technical systems, and business tradeoffs; willingness to ask questions, suggest ideas, and learn product strategy through hands-on execution.
  • Experience supporting product launches, release notes, customer education, or GTM coordination.

Compensation & Transparency

At Fingerprint, we believe in pay transparency — it’s part of how we operate as a distributed, remote-first team. Salaries are based on function, level, and geographic location, benchmarked against similar stage growth companies.

Because this role is open across the United States and can be based anywhere our team members work from, the salary range reflects that geographic breadth: $126k - $170k

Some example salaries for specific locations are below:

  • Chicago: $126k - $145k

Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors, including the successful candidate’s location, experience, and expertise, and may vary from the amounts listed above.

Additionally, because Fingerprint is an all-remote company and people can join our workforce from almost any country, we do not sponsor visas. Fingerprint teammates need to be authorized to work from their home location.

We are dedicated to creating an inclusive work environment for everyone. We embrace and celebrate the unique experiences, perspectives and cultural backgrounds that each employee brings to our workplace. Fingerprint strives to foster an environment where our employees feel respected, valued and empowered, and our team members are at the forefront in helping us promote and sustain an inclusive workplace. We’d still love to hear from you.

jobs.jd_full:
About Pacaso

Pacaso exists to enrich lives by making second home ownership possible and enjoyable for more people. We’ve reimagined the second home category — pairing a thoughtfully designed co-ownership model with simplified financials, equitable scheduling, and dedicated local property management, so owners get the joy of a true second home without the hassle.

Since launch, Pacaso has facilitated more than $1.2 billion in gross real estate transactions and service fees across 40+ destinations in the U.S., Mexico, and Europe — including Aspen, Lake Tahoe, Napa, Malibu, Palm Springs, Cabo, Paris, London, and most recently Florence, Milan, and Rome. We’ve raised over $300 million in cumulative equity funding, closed the largest real estate Regulation A+ offering of 2025, and reserved the Nasdaq ticker PCSO as we build toward a public listing.

Our work has been featured in The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, Fortune, Forbes, CNBC, Bloomberg, and others.

Recognition

We’re a Certified Great Place to Work and have been honored for both our culture and our category-defining work:

  • No. 5, Forbes America’s Best Startup Employers (2026) — our second consecutive Top 10 ranking
  • Newsweek’s America’s Greatest Startup Workplaces (2025)
  • Winner, 2025 Inman Best of Proptech Awards — Consumer Experience & Marketplace Innovation
  • Fortune & Great Place To Work Best Workplaces in Real Estate (2024)
  • Best Workplace in the Bay Area™ (2023)
  • LinkedIn Top Startup (2022) · Glassdoor Best Places to Work, #6 (2022)

The role

Pacaso buyers are high-net-worth individuals making a considered purchase over months, sometimes years. They move between our site, email, messaging, and our Sales team, and today each of those runs on its own tools with its own picture of the customer. We believe one personalized system that follows each customer from first interest to purchase, and keeps serving them as an owner, will shorten the path to purchase and make our growth product-led.

We’re hiring a principal-level technical product manager to own that system and its outcome. You’ll own the system-level design: the components, how they fit together, what the system decides and why, and how the AI agents behave. You’ll own the roadmap, and you’ll do hands-on work yourself: working prototypes built with AI tooling, UI design, and the prompts behind the agents. Engineering owns the technical design and implementation, and you shape and review it with them as it goes to production.

This is a technical product leadership role, not a backlog-management role and not a production engineering role. You’ll make product calls with Sales, Marketing, and leadership, work through system tradeoffs with senior engineers, and be accountable for the outcome.

Some of this is already moving. AI agents talk to our customers today, and parts of the data and decisioning exist. None of it runs end to end on its own yet. You’ll take what’s there, decide what to keep, and design the system that can.

What you’ll own

  • The system-level design. One design for new leads, dormant leads, and stalled buyers first, then owners who add a share, so the same person is served by one system instead of separate tools for each stage. You own the components, how they fit together, what the system decides and why, and the agent behavior and prompts. Engineering owns the technical design and implementation, and you shape and review it with them.
  • The customer intelligence layer. What the system knows about each customer across channels and how it acts on it: signals, shared memory and context, scoring, eligibility and frequency caps, and the next-best-action logic that decides what happens next.
  • Agent and workflow design. Which agents exist, what each one is allowed to decide, how they hand off to each other and to Sales, and the prompts, tools, and orchestration behind them.
  • Trust and reliability. Evaluation frameworks, guardrails, observability, cost and latency budgets, and kill switches, in place before anything reaches a customer.
  • The path to autonomy. What the system decides on its own, what still needs a person, and the evidence we need before we take that person out of the loop.
  • The roadmap. What gets built in what order, and why. You set priorities across the site, email, messaging, the CRM, and Sales handoffs, and work with Engineering on build-versus-buy decisions.
  • The outcome. Funnel velocity (time from first interest to high intent, and to purchase) and the measured lift in qualified actions and closed sales.

Two examples of the work:

  • An AI agent engages a new lead in the channel they prefer, qualifies them, and hands them to Sales at the right moment with the context Sales needs to close.
  • A customer reads an email, chats with us, and comes back to the site a week later. They get one continuous experience, because the system remembers what we’ve already said and done.

Who you are

  • Customer-obsessed. You start from the customer’s experience, not the org chart or the backlog. When you have to choose between channels, surfaces, or features, the tiebreaker is what improves that experience. Our customers value clarity and discretion, and you design for both.
  • A systems thinker who still builds. You think at the system level, and you still do the hands-on work: prototypes, UI design, and prompts. You’re expert at getting AI to do real work through prompting, tool use, and orchestration.
  • Technically deep. You can read a data model, question an integration design, reason about latency, cost, and failure modes, and be a credible partner to senior engineers as they make design decisions.
  • Rigorous about autonomy. You design systems to run on their own, and you know how to prove they’re ready. Evals and guardrails go in before launch, not after an incident.
  • Accountable for outcomes. You measure yourself on results, not tasks shipped. You’ve stopped your own work when the impact wasn’t there, and you can tell us about it.
  • Fluent in business and technical. You can frame and defend a tradeoff with Sales, Marketing, and leadership, then go deep with engineers on the build. You own the product and system decisions, and you can follow and shape the technical ones.
  • A multiplier. You raise the bar for how Product, Engineering, and Data build with AI, through your designs, your reviews, and the patterns you leave behind.
  • A partner. Marketing and Sales are core stakeholders, and you’ll co-own the buyer journey with our product owner for new-lead acquisition. When the path to impact runs through another team’s area, you work with the owner to move it.
  • Fast at context. You go deep on systems you didn’t build and turn a lot of information into a plan quickly.

What you’ll bring

We’ll ask for specific evidence of each of these. If you can’t point to all six, this probably isn’t the right fit yet.

  1. Customer obsession. You take customer insights and translate them into real product features that deliver results.
  2. A production agentic system. You’ve designed and shipped an autonomous or agentic system that runs end to end with minimal human intervention. You can show us what it decides on its own and how you knew it was making the right calls before you trusted it with real customers.
  3. A measurable growth outcome. You’ve owned a growth, conversion, lifecycle, or re-engagement result. You can give us the baseline, what you changed, the lift, the time frame, and how you knew your work caused it.
  4. Decisioning and intelligence layers. You’ve designed signals, identity, scoring, context, eligibility and caps, or next-best-action logic.
  5. Prototype to production. You’ve built working prototypes yourself with AI tooling, beyond specs and slides, and taken at least one to production with engineers. You can tell us what you owned and what they owned.
  6. Cross-team system design. You’ve owned the system-level design for a product that multiple teams built on or integrated with, and shaped the technical design with the engineers who owned it.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with long-consideration, high-value purchases such as real estate, luxury, or financial services.
  • Experience putting AI into a human sales team’s workflow, including CRM integration.
  • An earlier career as a software engineer, data architect, or solutions architect.

This role isn’t for you if

  • You want to execute against a defined spec, or manage a backlog someone else shaped.
  • You want to manage a team right now. This is a principal IC role.
  • You want to own the technical architecture and implementation. Engineering owns those here.
  • You see this as an email or campaign program, or measure success in opens, clicks, or campaigns shipped.
  • Your AI experience is mostly using it to write docs and emails faster.
  • You need a full team and a clean data stack before you start. Some pieces exist today and don’t talk to each other yet.

How we work

We start with AI. It’s one of our core values. We design processes with automation and intelligence in mind from the start, and our product team already has AI agents talking to customers.

Small team, real ownership. Product at Pacaso works closely with Engineering, Design, Data, Sales, and Marketing. If you see a problem worth solving, you’re trusted to solve it. We ship weekly and demo working software, not slides.

We move fast and play the long game. We make decisions and change course quickly. “Embrace an infinite mindset” is one of our values: a quarterly number is information, not a verdict, and we’d rather send nothing than send the wrong thing.

We pick up the phone and empty the dishwasher. When async isn’t enough, we get on a call. No task is beneath anyone, and we keep bureaucracy to a minimum. We’re a distributed Crew.

Compensation

  • Around $200,000- $225,000k depending on location and experience with equity (RSU’s)

 

Why You’ll Love Working Here

We invest in our Crew the way we invest in our homes — thoughtfully, generously, and with care.

  • Competitive base salary and meaningful equity — every Crew member shares in what we’re building
  • Discretionary time off — take the rest you need, when you need it
  • Premium medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your family
  • Sponsored memberships to One Medical, Peloton, and WellHub for whole-person, modern healthcare
  • 401(k) to help you build long-term security
  • Paid parental leave for primary and secondary caregivers
  • Home office stipend and a monthly internet and cell phone reimbursement to set you up for great remote work
  • Quarterly team gatherings and ongoing learning and development investment

Our Commitment

Pacaso is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, ability, and background — including veterans and individuals with disabilities. We believe a Crew as diverse as the owners we serve makes Pacaso stronger, and we’re committed to building a workplace where every voice belongs.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager – Platform & Data
jobs.jd_full:
Own the platform underneath safetyOS™: the shared services and data every Securly product runs on.

Securly keeps students safe in 27,000+ schools, and our technology has helped save 2,400+ student lives. Nine products run on one platform. We’re hiring a Senior Product Manager – Platform & Data to make it work as one system for every district.

THE ROLE

You’ll own strategy and the roadmap across three layers:

  • Core platform services: SSO, SIS and rostering integrations through Sync, and data acquisition, with real availability and SLO accountability.
  • Data platform: you own the product requirements for our layered data pipeline, from raw district data to clean, trusted data every product uses. Our Data team owns how it’s built.
  • Customer-facing data products: the data marts, APIs and reporting district leaders act on.

You’ll work with our CTO, Engineering in the U.S. and Pune, the Data team, product leads for every product line, and Customer Success.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Set the strategy and roadmap across platform services, the data platform and data products.
  • Define and hold SLOs for SSO, SIS integrations and data acquisition.
  • Own SIS integrations and data acquisition so rostering data arrives reliably from every district.
  • Define what each pipeline layer delivers, from raw ingestion to curated data, and set data quality standards with the Data team.
  • Own shared metrics and data models, so terms like “active student” and “screen time” mean the same thing in every product.
  • Build in student data privacy: FERPA, COPPA and state privacy laws shape every data decision.
  • Ship data products districts use directly, from discovery to adoption.
  • Decide what’s built once for the platform and what stays with each product.
  • Make onboarding one step: one setup, every product working together.
  • Stay close to customers: district IT directors and administrators shape your roadmap.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

  • 90 days: You’ve mapped our data flows, met key partners, and set SLO targets and a first roadmap.
  • 6 months: You run platform planning, and product teams build on your standards.
  • 12 months: You can show faster onboarding, higher uptime and cross-product reporting districts trust.

WHAT YOU BRING

Must have

  • 7+ years in product management, including end-to-end ownership of a data platform product
  • Layered data architecture: raw data lands, gets cleaned and standardized, then becomes curated data ready for reporting. Medallion (bronze, silver, gold) is a plus; lakehouse, data warehouse or similar staged pipelines count too.
  • Data modeling and shared metric definitions across multiple products or data sources
  • Customer-facing data products: data marts, APIs or reporting
  • Shared runtime services with SLO accountability
  • Based in the U.S. and authorized to work without visa sponsorship

Strongly preferred

  • Student data privacy: FERPA, COPPA and state privacy laws, or comparable regulated data such as HIPAA
  • K-12 SIS and rostering: PowerSchool, Infinite Campus, Clever, ClassLink or OneRoster
  • Ingestion and sync from many external sources at scale
  • Identity and SSO: SAML, OIDC, Google and Microsoft sign-in

Nice to have

  • K-12 EdTech experience

WHO YOU ARE

  • You think in data flows and catch quality issues before customers do.
  • You lead through influence and make the teams around you better.
  • You’re credible in both rooms: deep with data engineers, clear with executives.
  • You use AI daily and know where it helps.

WHY SECURLY

  • Top-tier medical, dental and vision coverage
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Unlimited PTO plus a paid year-end shutdown
  • 12 weeks of paid parental leave
  • Free 24⁄7 confidential mental health counseling and wellness tools
  • $1,000 annual learning stipend
  • Structured onboarding and ongoing coaching

Our people-first culture shows in the numbers: 82% employee engagement against a 73% global benchmark, and 94% of employees proud to work here (Securly Qualtrics Employee Survey, 2025; WSA Global Benchmark).

ABOUT SECURLY

Securly launched the first cloud-based K-12 web filter in 2013. Today safetyOS™ covers everything a district needs to keep students safe, secure and ready to learn:

  • Unified Experience: single sign-on, SIS integrations and self-deployment
  • Digital Safety: filtering that handles 20% of U.S. K-12 internet traffic
  • AI Governance: guardrails and visibility as students use AI
  • Student Wellness: 24⁄7 monitoring with human-verified alerts
  • Classroom Management: classroom, device and flex period management
  • Campus Movement: 2 million digital hall passes created every day
  • Family Engagement: visibility for parents into their child’s digital life
  • Digital Insights: reporting on tech and AI use, screen time and circumvention

Every one of these runs on the platform this role owns.

Working in the Office of the Chief Medical Officer and reporting to the VP of Point of Care & Risk Stratification, the Senior Director of Strategy & Operations, Point of Care, will lead day-to-day operations, partnerships, go-to-market efforts, and wraparound support services to maximize the impact of Aledade’s value-based care insights to our partner practices. 

The team is looking for a high-output generalist with a strong business analyst toolkit, looking to rapidly take ownership of complex content with high visibility, working across multiple stakeholders. Candidates that thrive managing multiple deadlines on tight timelines and learning content quickly are best positioned to succeed; successful team members in the same function primarily have backgrounds in consulting and generalist healthcare strategy & operations roles.

To start, the role will focus on 1) scaling the deployment of our point of care tools and 2) broadening and deepening the insights available in our point of care tools, to maximize the impact of Aledade’s insights on our patients’ health outcomes and partner practices’ success in their value-based care contracts. 

At the end of their first year, a successful leader in the role will own end-to-end accountability for 1) proactive identification, development, and execution of Point of Care deployment improvement opportunities, including field, practice, and clinician education, deployment automation and monitoring, and go to market approach and materials, 2) strategic relationship building and partnership with Aledade’s payer partners to advance point of care tool adoption and impact, 3) goal setting, metric identification and development, and impact evaluation for our point of care tools, 4) identification, evaluation, contracting, and cross-functional execution of net new vendor and external partnerships that support insight delivery and impact.

Additionally, this role will 1) provide direction and expert guidance to junior team members owning individual initiatives, including incentive and adoption programs, educational efforts, hotspotting, monitoring, and alerting development, practice and user-level prioritization and triage, and 2) coordinate with cross-functional product, analytics, technology, performance, care programs, and other senior leaders across Aledade to advance point of care tool adoption and impact.

The role is expected to start as a senior individual contributor, but is expected to grow into a people manager in the near term.

Primary Duties:

In collaboration with cross-functional product, analytics, technology, performance, care programs, and other senior leaders across Aledade:

  1. Own single-threaded accountability for proactive identification, development, and execution of Point of Care deployment improvement opportunities, including field, practice, and clinician education, deployment automation and monitoring, and go to market approach and materials
  2. Lead strategic relationship building and partnership with Aledade’s payer partners to advance point of care tool adoption and impact

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s Degree required, preferably in Economics, Business, Healthcare, or a related field
  • 12+ years of progressive professional experience, or 7+ years progressive professional experience with a Master’s Degree, strongly preferred
  • 6+ years of experience in healthcare
  • 2+ years of experience in value-based care

  • Expert Excel skills required, including the ability to work with large, complex, & often incomplete data sets; conduct one-off complex analyses quickly; and utilize Index / Match, XLOOKUP, FILTER, and other advanced formulas
  • Advanced PPT skills required, including storyboarding skills, ability to translate complex analyses and concepts into engaging slides, and ability to draft executive-level materials with limited direction
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, as well as the ability to build strong relationships and work with individuals at all levels of the organization, tailoring communication style as appropriate based on audience
  • Excellent project management skills, including proven track record leading complex, cross-functional initiatives in health care operations settings
  • Strong strategic planning and analytical skills
  • Strong “business analyst” toolkit, including abilities to independently prioritize, solve problems via hypothesis-driven analytical methods, manage across multiple responsibilities and projects, execute with attention to detail, and overcome ambiguity
  • Poise, confidence, and maturity interacting with key stakeholders, including senior leaders
  • Commitment to confidentiality and discretion in appropriately handling sensitive information is required

Sitting for prolonged periods of time. Extensive use of computers and keyboard. Occasional walking and lifting may be required.

Aledade PBC, a public benefit corporation, exists to empower the most transformational part of our health care landscape - independent primary care. We were founded in 2014, and since then, we’ve become the largest network of independent primary care in the country - helping practices, health centers and clinics deliver better care to their patients and thrive in value-based care. Additionally, by creating value-based contracts across a wide variety of health plans, we aim to flip the script on the traditional fee-for-service model. Our work strengthens continuity of care, aligns incentives and ensures primary care physicians are paid for what they do best - keeping patients healthy. If you want to help create a health care system that is good for patients, good for practices and good for society - and if you’re eager to join a collaborative, inclusive and remote-first culture - you’ve come to the right place.
